## Definitions

- [statement] Parkin is an E3 ligase that functions together with the ubiquitin kinase PINK1 to flag damaged mitochondria for removal via a selective form of autophagy known as mitophagy. (high confidence) — https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ady0240 · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24896179/
- [statement] Mutations in the Parkin and PINK1 proteins are the most common form of autosomal recessive PD. (high confidence) — https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ady0240 · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789816/
- [statement] pS65-Ubiquitin (pUb) is a PINK1 substrate, and a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant page says the differential effectiveness of PINK1 activator compounds will be determined by analyzing specific biomarkers. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11100876/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/grant/pink1-activators-treating-parkinsons-disease

## Structure and components

- [statement] ClinicalTrials.gov lists Parts 1-4 of the MTX325 study as complete, and Mission reports that in a completed Phase 1a SAD/MAD study in healthy volunteers, MTX325 demonstrated high CNS penetration, while a PET study confirmed distribution into brain parenchyma. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07630545 · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/

## How it works

- [statement] Mission states that its MTX325-101 Phase 1b study is designed to establish clinical proof-of-mechanism using a wide range of biomarkers and imaging measures, and the registry's official title for NCT07630545 includes assessing CNS penetration, biodistribution, and biomarkers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07630545

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Mission Therapeutics announced that the first patient has been dosed in its Phase 1b proof-of-mechanism study of MTX325, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists Part 5 (multiple doses in patients with Parkinson's Disease) as in progress. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07630545

## Facts and statements

- [statement] USP30, a deubiquitinase localized to mitochondria, antagonizes mitophagy driven by the ubiquitin ligase parkin and the protein kinase PINK1. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24896179/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/
- [statement] One study reports that knockdown of USP30 rescues the defective mitophagy caused by pathogenic mutations in parkin, and another reports that USP30 inhibition promoted mitophagy in PARK2 KO neurons. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24896179/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789816/
- [statement] In an αSyn-induced model, Usp30 knockout mice are reported to show protection against behavioral deficits, increased mitophagy, decreased phospho-S129 αSyn, and attenuation of SN dopaminergic neuronal loss. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10643470/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/
- [statement] The authors report that the observations in knockout mice were recapitulated with MTX115325, a potent, selective, brain-penetrant USP30 inhibitor. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10643470/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11751875/
- [statement] Reports differ on MTK458: a preprint describes a brain penetrant small molecule that binds to PINK1 and stabilizes its active complex, while Science Advances authors report that MTK458 induces mild mitochondrial stress through PINK1/Parkin-independent off-target activities. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11100876/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ady0240
- [statement] One study reports that basal mammalian mitophagy occurs independently of PINK1, whereas another reports that the age-dependent rise in Drosophila mitophagy is abrogated by PINK1 or parkin deficiency. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5807059/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://elifesciences.org/articles/35878
- [statement] AbbVie acquired Mitokinin in 2023, and AbbVie described Mitokinin's lead compound as a selective PINK1 activator designed to address mitochondrial dysfunction. (medium confidence) — https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/abbv-1088 · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbvie-exercises-exclusive-right-to-acquire-mitokinin-further-strengthening-neuroscience-pipeline-301946322.html
- [statement] Mission states that recruitment is ongoing for 36 participants with mild to moderate idiopathic PD and that a data readout is anticipated in late 2027. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15) — https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/ · keywords: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30

## Research summary — Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30

PINK1 (a ubiquitin kinase) and parkin (an E3 ligase) flag damaged mitochondria for mitophagy, and mutations in both are linked to autosomal recessive PD. USP30, a mitochondrial deubiquitinase, opposes this pathway. Preclinical mouse and human-neuron studies support USP30 inhibition; Mission Therapeutics reports its USP30 inhibitor MTX325 has reached patients with PD in a Phase 1b study. PINK1 activators such as MTK458 are earlier-stage, and a Science Advances paper reports PINK1/Parkin-independent off-target effects for two activators.

## Source disagreement — Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
